explanation: Its ear openings sit at slightly different heights, so a squeak reaches each ear at a different moment and volume, letting it pinpoint prey up, down and sideways.

claims.text: Barn owls can locate and catch prey in complete darkness using hearing alone.
Kestrels, golden eagles and peregrine falcons hunt by sight and cannot catch prey in total darkness.
A barn owl's ear openings are set at different heights on its head.
The difference lets a barn owl locate sounds vertically as well as horizontally.
